title: The Battle of Hastings
about: when it happened, who fought and where. Include several specific numbers, dates or names where the topic has them, some exact and some rounded or hedged (about, nearly, more than, up to).
passages: The Battle of Hastings was fought on 14 October 1066, on a low ridge about 7 miles from the town of Hastings in southern England. On one side stood Harold Godwinson, the English king, who had been crowned only that January. On the other was William, Duke of Normandy, who believed the English throne had been promised to him. The Normans were DESCENDANTS of Viking settlers who had made a new home in northern France. Over time they took up the French language and became famous for fighting on horseback. William crossed the Channel with perhaps 7,000 men and landed at Pevensey on 28 September.

Harold arrived tired. Less than three weeks earlier he had beaten a Norwegian army at Stamford Bridge, and then he marched his troops more than 200 miles south. His soldiers, including his best fighters, the HOUSECARLS, locked their shields together into a wall along the hilltop. Norman archers and CAVALRY charged again and again for nearly nine hours. Late in the day Harold was killed, and the English line broke. William was crowned in Westminster Abbey on Christmas Day. The whole story is stitched into the Bayeux TAPESTRY, an embroidered cloth about 70 metres long that can still be seen in France today.
